page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache resources include 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 38 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with an exceptionally high memory capacity of 219.0 GB, translating to 54.69 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 262 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark results indicate that the M8-4ms prioritizes memory capacity over raw processing speed. CPU performance is relatively low, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1035.08 and a multi-core score of 2724.76. Geekbench testing aligns with these results, yielding a single-core score of 885.0 and a multi-core score of 1970.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 151.25 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 17.71 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database and application performance benchmarks reflect these constraints, with Redis SET operations reaching 2.63 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 3.0 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a specialized trade-off, offering massive memory density per vCPU rather than high-performance compute resources. It is designed for workloads that require large in-memory datasets but have modest CPU requirements. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive databases, large-scale caching layers, and enterprise applications that demand substantial RAM footprints without intensive parallel processing needs.
